newsitem.title: USA: Cigarette makers file to appeal FDA ruling.
newsitem.headline: Cigarette makers file to appeal FDA ruling.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. said Thursday it and other major U.S. tobacco companies have filed a notice of intent to appeal a North Carolina judge's ruling that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has jurisdiction to regulate tobacco as a drug.
Nat Walker, a spokesman for RJR Nabisco unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., said the notice was filed in the 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Richmond, Va.
"It was filed Tuesday afternoon," Walker said. "It was all the defendants."

U.S. District Judge William Osteen Sr. ruled in North Carolina on April 25 that the FDA has the power to regulate cigarettes and other products containing nicotine. He agreed with the FDA that nicotine was addictive and that cigarettes were drug delivery systems.
But Osteen ruled that the FDA did not have authority to regulate cigarette advertising and promotions.
Major tobacco companies had been widely expected to appeal the ruling. (--Jane Sutton, 305-374-5013)
